transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-23 17:00 UTC · Duration 45m · Attendees: Avery, Samira, Daniel, Maria, Ethan

00:00 Avery: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is the weekly latency tune sync for Rivermark, I'll hand it over to Samira to kick off with the latest numbers
00:10 Samira: yeah thanks, quick recap — last week we ran three suites, non-streaming and streaming, with seq lengths 256/512/1024, and we tried flash attention and fused cuda kernels, plus int8-ish quant on the 7b variant
00:23 Daniel: when you say int8-ish, are you referring to the model quant profile you recommended? we got a little confused between the redwood-optimized 7b-q and the floating variant
00:30 Samira: right, the profile is rwood-opt-7b-int8 — sorry that auto transcribed wrong earlier — it's a per-layer dynamic quant, not static 8-bit across all ops so quality hold is fine
00:40 Maria: reminder, for our VPC staging we need the config we used, otherwise we can't repro the KV cache warmups
00:46 Avery: noted, we'll include the exact start command and envs in the sheet
00:50 01:05 Samira: TTFT numbers first: with cold KV and non-streaming 512 seq our p50 to first token was about 320ms on a single A100-80g equivalent; with streaming enabled that dropped to ~160ms after initial chunking, and with warmed KV cache we see 90–110ms p50 TTFT
01:23 Ethan: can you clarify warm cache — is that prefix caching across requests or internal kv-cache per connection? we run many short requests so caches might not persist
01:32 Samira: good question — we mean both. prefix cache for repeated prompts and kv-cache re-use for multi-turn. For your workload, since you have many short single-turn calls, the benefit is smaller unless you enable request batching or a short TTL on the prefix cache
01:45 Daniel: what's the overhead of streaming itself? we worry streaming might increase p99 on token 1 because of chunk negotiation or extra hops
01:52 Samira: streaming adds a small protocol overhead but it lets us emit tokens as soon as the decoder computes the first chunk. In our tests streaming decreased time-to-first-token consistently versus non-streaming, although end-to-end tail latency can vary if jitter's present on the network
02:08 Maria: kernel choices — you mentioned flash attention gave better throughput, but fused kernels better p99, could you repeat? the notes had some mismatch
02:15 Samira: yes, flash-att (flash attention) reduces memory pressure and boosts throughput for longer seqs; fused cuda kernels (we used fused-gemm + fused-attn) improved stability and tail latency especially at seq <=512. For 1024 seq the flash kernels had higher throughput but slightly worse p99 for small batch sizes
02:36 Daniel: so practical recommendation for us, which is mostly 300–600 tokens per request, and bursty QPS of up to 45 QPS — what kernel + batch profile do we pick?
02:44 Samira: for 300–600 we'd recommend fused kernels plus streaming on the hosted path for lowest TTFT; for dedicated GPU pools with higher batch capacity, flash attention with a small group batcher is better to lower cost per token while keeping latency SLOs
02:59 Ethan: are there quantization regressions? we cannot accept any hallucination increase or quality drops on regulatory text
03:06 Samira: we ran evals on your regulatory prompt set with the int8-ish profile and saw negligible delta in BLEU/rouge-type metrics; we'll share the eval artifacts. still we recommend a short AB test and hold a regression threshold before flipping to int8 in prod
03:20 03:35 Avery: security asks — Maria, you had SOC2/SSO questions last time? we attached the SOC2 summary in the repo earlier but will push the full pack after this call
03:42 Maria: yes we need audit log retention details and KMS flow for the private deployment. also confirm that dedicated instances can be pinned to our VPC and that keys never leave HSM
03:52 Samira: yes, for Private deployments keys are customer-managed via KMS/HSM and audit logs are retained per our enterprise package. We'll include a diagram and specifics in the security pack
04:05 Daniel: back to perf — what's the expected TTFT delta if we move from hosted API to dedicated with reserved capacity?
04:12 Samira: reserved capacity reduces variability: we measured ~15–25% improvement on p95 and p99 over shared-hosted under similar batch settings, primarily because you remove noisy neighbors and we can tune kernel residency and pre-warm kv caches more aggressively
04:28 Daniel: could you run a dedicated-vpc run so we can see apples-to-apples with our network path?
04:33 Avery: yes we can schedule a VPC/staging perf run. Maria, what's your available window?
04:36 Maria: staging's open Tue/Wed next week after 08:00 UTC, I'd prefer Tue 2027-11-30 09:00 UTC
04:44 Avery: I'll book that and include Samira for the test and an infra handshake beforehand
04:49 05:00 Samira: plan for the benchmark: we'll run 3 workloads — short (avg 200 tokens), medium (avg 450 tokens), long (avg 900 tokens). For each we'll run non-streaming cold, streaming cold, streaming warmed-KV, and vary batch sizes 1,4,8. We'll produce TTFT, p50/p95/p99 token-latency, and throughput numbers. For kernel selection we'll try fused-gemm+fused-attn and flash-attn and capture which gave best p99 per workload
05:25 Ethan: please include raw logs and kernel toggles, we want to plug into our tracing to see where time is spent
05:30 Samira: will do; we'll also include the exact docker/image tag and runtime flags so you can repro locally if needed
05:38 Daniel: one more question — do you have a knob to force streaming chunk size? our clients have very strict first-response windows, we'd like a smaller chunk to push TTFT lower
05:45 Samira: yes chunking is configurable; smaller chunks reduce first-token latency but increase token-generation overhead. there's a sweet spot we can find for your prompt distribution — we'll tune it in the 512-stream test
05:55 Maria: any concerns about network RTT in our VPC adding noise? we saw 20–40ms variance on egress path last month
06:02 Samira: we'll run repeated iterations and include network-only baselines; if needed we can propose colocated infra for dedicated runs or use an edge node to mitigate RTT
06:14 Avery: recap — Redwood to run streaming benchmark focused on 512 seq warmed and cold, include TTFT and p50/p95/p99, try fused vs flash kernels, include quant evals and raw logs; Rivermark to provide traces and QPS targets; schedule VPC run for 2027-11-30; security pack and pricing to be shared by 2027-11-24
06:36 Daniel: that works, thanks. any blockers on Redwood side?
06:40 Samira: none, just need the traces and access window from Maria. We'll try to prioritize the 512 streaming run first
06:46 Avery: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the sheet and invite for the VPC test.
06:50 Meeting end

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard model names (rwood-opt vs redwood-opt), 'KV cache' sometimes appears as 'k v cash' in auto-transcript. Natural crosstalk and filler words present.
